Plain-language definitions of the treasury, cash management, and AI-finance terms that matter. A B C D I L R T A Accounting Reconciliation Accounting reconciliation is the act of comparing two sets of financial records to ensure they match. AI Cash Flow Forecasting AI cash flow forecasting uses real-time data, pattern recognition, and continuous learning to predict future cash positions and flag potential liquidity issues before they happen. Autonomous Finance Agents Autonomous Finance Agents are AI-driven systems embedded in finance and treasury ecosystems that don't just follow fixed rules, they also make decisions, perceiving, reasoning, and acting often without human intervention. B Bank Connectivity Bank connectivity refers to the systems, pipes, and protocols that allow companies to communicate directly with their banks. Bank Reconciliation Automation Bank reconciliation automation uses technology to automatically match bank transactions against internal financial records in real time, eliminating manual cross-referencing and flagging only the exceptions that need attention. C Cash Balance The cash balance is simply the amount of liquid assets available in company accounts at a given point in time. Cash Concentration Cash concentration is the process of sweeping funds from multiple bank accounts into a central account, usually managed at the group or holding company level. Cash Conversion Cycle The cash conversion cycle (CCC) is a financial metric that measures how long it takes for a business to convert its operational investments, like project work, infrastructure, or customer acquisition, into cash received from clients. Cash Flow Liquidity Ratio The cash flow liquidity ratio measures your company's ability to cover its short-term liabilities with the cash it generates from operations. Cash Flow Planning Cash flow planning is the art and science of projecting how money moves into and out of a business. Cash Visibility Cash visibility is exactly what it sounds like - the ability to clearly see where your cash is, in real time, across all your accounts and entities. Corporate Treasury Management Corporate treasury management is treasury run at enterprise scale: overseeing liquidity, funding, investments, and financial risk across multiple legal entities, banks, and currencies. D Daily Bank Reconciliation Daily bank reconciliation is the process of matching your internal records with what the bank shows - every single day. Digital Treasury Digital treasury refers to the use of modern technologies to automate, streamline, and elevate treasury management. I Invoice Matching Invoice matching is the process of comparing supplier invoices against related documents - like purchase orders (POs) and goods received notes - to ensure consistency before payment is approved. L Liquidity Planning Liquidity planning is about answering: do we have enough cash to meet our obligations, and when will we need more? R Real-Time Cash Flow Forecasting Real-time cash flow forecasting provides up-to-the-minute visibility into a company's liquidity by tapping into live data sources to deliver continuously updated cash projections. Real-Time Cash Position A real-time cash position gives finance teams instant, live visibility into a company's available cash across every bank account, entity, and currency, right now rather than as of yesterday's report. Rolling Cash Forecast A rolling cash forecast is a continuously updating projection that shifts forward as time passes, rather than remaining static. T Treasury Management Treasury management is the practice of overseeing a company's cash, liquidity, funding, and financial risk so the business always has the right money in the right place at the right time. Treasury Management System A treasury management system (TMS) is, in essence, the strategic control room for a company's cash, liquidity, and risk posture.
